blinds_now_summary.title: Starter setup
blinds_now_summary.description:
{blinds}

At night, nothing moves.
During the day, each blind closes partway (to position {shade_position}, tilt {shade_tilt}) whenever the sun is shining on its own side of the house, and stays fully open (position {open_position}) the rest of the time.

Continue to create it as shown, or cancel this setup and start over from the main menu.

user.title: Add guard
user.description: Which policy, and where in the order. The policy decides which fields the next screen has, so it is asked first.

data_description.policy: No default on purpose: the three policies do three different things.
data_description.order: Lower is tried first. Suggested as ten past the last guard, leaving room to slip one in between two later on. Two guards cannot share an order.

guard.title: Add guard
guard.description: Guards are tried in order and the first one that matches wins. A guard can skip a movement, defer it, or force a different action instead.

data.targets: What it covers (leave empty for every blind in the house)
data.condition_ref: Named condition (leave empty to build one inline, or for a guard that always applies)
data.when: Inline condition (leave empty if using a named condition, or for a guard that always applies)

data_description.targets: Blinds and zones, mixed freely. Empty means every blind -- there is no difference here between 'unset' and 'all'.
data_description.applies_to: 'closing' means a falling position, not the slats. Most guards in a house are 'closing', but the default stays 'any' so a guard means the same thing however it was written.
data_description.stage: 'after the decision' overrides the action; 'before the decision' drops the target out of the decision entirely. A guard acting before the decision must use 'any' -- there is no command yet whose direction it could mean.
data_description.condition_ref: A numeric threshold can only be reached this way: Home Assistant's inline condition selector rejects the fallback value this integration requires, so name a condition instead.
data_description.position: Pick 'keep' to leave this axis alone, pick a configured value to read the number from that helper, or type a number from 0 to 100.
data_description.tilt: Pick 'keep' to leave this axis alone, pick a configured value to read the number from that helper, or type a number from 0 to 100.
data_description.wait_limit: 'no limit' is a real answer, not a blank one: it waits until the condition clears. There is deliberately no default -- the two choices do different things.
data_description.max_wait_duration: Only read when 'at most' is chosen. Left at zero, the guard is refused rather than saved as a zero-second wait.
data_description.on_timeout: No default on purpose: dropping the movement and doing it anyway are opposites.
data_description.recheck_every: A deferred movement does not survive a Home Assistant restart, so this is the safety net that picks it up again.

import_export.title: Import / export configuration
import_export.description: Reads or writes the whole configuration as a YAML file -- the same import_config/export_config services Developer Tools can call directly.

execution.title: Execution
execution.description: Whether this integration actually moves the covers, or only writes to the log what it would have moved. Dry run is the safe setting: every command is logged with the service and payload it would have used, so a day of it can be compared against the automations it replaces. Turning it off gives this integration hands.

data_description.dry_run: On: nothing is moved, every intended command is written to the log. Off: covers really move. This takes effect immediately, with no reload.

fixture_drift.title: Configuration no longer matches fixtures/dom_peter.yaml
fixture_drift.description: The blinds, zones, modes, conditions, values or rules configured here no longer match `fixtures/dom_peter.yaml` in this checkout -- the file the 92,160-scenario migration gate measures. Differing: {fields}. Re-import that file (the `import_config` service) to bring the two back together, or update the fixture to match the configuration you actually intend, before trusting the gate again.

unknown_entities.title: Configuration references entities this Home Assistant does not have
unknown_entities.description: {count} entity or entities named by this configuration exist in neither the state machine nor the entity registry, so nothing here can read or command them: {entities}. A rule, condition or guard that depends on one will behave as though that input were absent, and a blind among them can never be moved. Create the missing helpers and entities, or edit the configuration to name the ones this house actually has. Checked once, after Home Assistant has finished starting.

blinds_missing_features.title: A blind cannot do what the rules ask of it
blinds_missing_features.description: {count} blind(s) named by this configuration lack cover features the rules need: {blinds}. The Home Assistant entity picker filters on the `cover` domain and nothing else, so a garage door or an awning can be chosen as a blind -- and the commands it cannot carry out are dropped silently. Either pick a cover that supports the listed features, or change the rules so they only ask for what it can do: 0 and 100 need only open and close, any value between needs the position setter. Checked once, after Home Assistant has finished starting.

blinds_without_zone.title: A blind belongs to no zone
blinds_without_zone.description: {count} blind(s) are configured and no zone claims them: {blinds}. Zones are how a rule reaches a blind, so nothing decides these and nothing will command them -- they are absent from the targets on the diagnostic sensor. Put each one in a zone, or remove it from the configuration. Every other blind keeps being decided meanwhile: this used to refuse the whole integration, which meant one incomplete blind stopped the rest working.
